is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (specifically An. coluzzii and An. gambiae) from Ebolowa, Cameroon.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-West), Vgsc L995S (kdr-East), and N1575Y (N1570Y).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides genotype frequencies for L1014F (kdr-West) in Figure 4 and associated text (page 6, section 3.4).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from field sites in Ebolowa, Cameroon (page 3, section 2.2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field collection and laboratory analysis.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies Ebolowa, South Cameroon (page 3, section 2.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was conducted between September and October 2021 (page 3, section 2.2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new, specific collection in Ebolowa in 2021.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. from Ebolowa, Cameroon. The population was found to be resistant to pyrethroids but susceptible to carbamates and organophosphates. Genotyping revealed the presence of the L1014F (kdr-West) mutation at a high frequency, which was significantly associated with survival in permethrin and alphacypermethrin bioassays.
